english.title: Channel tunnel - threaten to endanger train / system
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) threatened that you or another would

(A)_[destroy a Channel Tunnel train]_
(B)_[destroy goods on a Channel Tunnel train]_
(C)_[commit an act of violence on a Channel Tunnel train]_
(D)_[destroy the Channel Tunnel system]_
(E)_[destroy goods within the Channel Tunnel system]_
(F)_[commit an act of violence within the Channel Tunnel system]_

in order to compel **(..SPECIFY..) to do or abstain from doing an act and the making of the threat was likely to endanger the

(G)_[safe operation of the train]_
(H)_[safety of the tunnel system]_
(I)_[safe operation of the train or the tunnel system]_
english.legislation: Contrary to article 8(1) of the Channel Tunnel (Security) Order 1994.

investigatoraction.description: Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Consent of the Attorney General required, see article 9(1) of the Channel Tunnel (Security) Order 1994.
(ii) Terrorist connection - this offence is listed in Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 2020. Where the court has determined that there is a terrorist connection, the court has to treat this as an aggravating factor in sentencing (section 69 of that Act) and the notification requirements under the Counter-Terrorism Act 2008 apply (section 42 of that Act). In addition, section 23A of the Terrorism Act 2000 provides for forfeiture of money or other property
